name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 65

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: He is in a health-giving occupation

definitions.text: He is in a health-giving occupation

blocks.note: surface reading: a job that makes people well, like a doctor or nurse
setter's reading: a job of calling for people's health, as in raising glasses and saying 'Your health!'

explanation.walkthrough: A TOASTMASTER announces the toasts at a banquet, and a toast is a drink to someone's health, so he 'gives' healths all evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of ceremonies at a formal dinner calls the toasts, each one a wish of good health to someone.

clue.text: Dogged, but couldn't keep up with the others

definitions.text: couldn't keep up with the others

blocks.note: first meaning: followed closely, shadowed

blocks.clueFragment: couldn't keep up with the others
blocks.note: second meaning: lagged behind the rest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' reads as the adjective for persistent, but it is the past tense of the verb to dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both following someone's track and falling behind, so both clue halves fit its past tense.

clue.text: Where to see runners, as on a bed

blocks.note: taken as written
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Runners on a bed suggests bean plants or a cloth strip laid along a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The runners are racehorses; ASCOT is a famous racecourse near Windsor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a racecourse, a place to watch the horses entered in each race, which are called runners.

clue.text: International contest won by gifted horse

definitions.text: International contest won by gifted horse

blocks.note: surface reading: a talented horse winning an international race or show
setter's reading: the wooden horse given to Troy as a gift, which hid Greek soldiers and won the war

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' means talented on the surface, but the horse was literally a gift, left for the Trojans in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary conflict between Greeks and Trojans was ended by the ruse of the wooden horse.

clue.text: A mother may be the making of a man

blocks.note: taken as written
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A proverb-like saying that a good mother shapes her son into a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first man in the Bible, the man in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first human male, so he is the man par excellence.

clue.text: He rooted for reform, being a Roosevelt

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are shaped anew

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A US president from the Roosevelt family championed reform, as the Progressive one famously did.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th US president, so his first name picks out one member of that family.

clue.text: A fringe gathering of lace makers

definitions.text: A fringe gathering of lace makers

blocks.note: surface reading: a small side meeting of people who make lace, like a fringe event at a conference
setter's reading: a fabric gathering, a pleated or frilled strip of lace used as trimming

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' sounds like a meeting, but in dressmaking a gathering is fabric drawn into folds; a RUCHE is just such a frill of lace or net.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered strip of lace, chiffon or ribbon sewn on as a decorative trim or edging.

clue.text: Practice at home ground

blocks.note: a habit is a regular practice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports team trains at its own stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home ground' sounds like a team's stadium, but it is the natural home of an animal or plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a species lives, its native territory.

clue.text: You do what you like with it

definitions.text: You do what you like with it

blocks.note: surface reading: some object or tool you can use however you please
setter's reading: the capacity by which you choose your own actions, possessed by everyone

explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' sounds like a thing in your hand; it is the faculty of choice itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Free will is the power to act by one's own choice rather than by necessity or fate.

clue.text: City road

blocks.note: first meaning: the largest city in Alaska
second meaning: a sheltered stretch of water where ships ride at anchor, called roads or a roadstead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Road' reads as a street, but in nautical use roads are an offshore place where ships anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alaskan port city bears the name, and the common noun means a mooring place, the sailor's sense of road.

clue.text: Bill turns to Robert — "got a bean?"

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the carob tree bears a bean

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the bill's abbreviation is read from its end

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Rob is a short form of the name Robert

explanation.surface: Bill asks his friend Robert whether he has a spare penny, 'bean' being old slang for a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: CAROB is a tree whose pods give the carob bean, so it has 'got a bean'.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean tree famous for its edible pods, used as a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: All the difference between life and death?

definitions.text: All the difference between life and death?

blocks.clueFragment: All the difference between life and death?
blocks.note: surface reading: something that decides whether one survives, a vital matter

blocks.clueFragment: All the difference between life and death?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a description of a quality that turns the living into the dead

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like praise for something crucial; read literally it is whatever tips life into death, which is what a deadly dose does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of killing is what moves a person from being alive to being dead.

clue.text: Fan sticking?

definitions.note: adjective; the question mark admits the stretch

blocks.note: first meaning: a supporter or follower
second meaning: clinging or holding fast, as glue does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan sticking' suggests a jammed electric fan; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a loyal supporter; as an adjective it describes something clinging to a surface.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge uproar about broadcast

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the noise word wraps around the other one

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise
to broadcast seed is to sow it, scattering it widely by hand

explanation.surface: Someone declines to admit there was an outcry over a programme that went out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' tempts as radio or TV, but it is the farmer's sense of scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to deny any connection with or responsibility for something.

clue.text: Results of being quick on the draw

definitions.text: Results of being quick on the draw

blocks.note: surface reading: a gunfighter fast at pulling a pistol from the holster
setter's reading: an artist making rapid drawings

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom belongs to Wild West gunfights; here 'draw' means making pictures, and fast drawings are rough outlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketches are quick, rough drawings, the output of an artist working fast.

clue.text: One ordered to be silent

blocks.note: surface reading: someone commanded to keep quiet, like a scolded child
setter's reading: a member of a religious order whose rule keeps its monks largely silent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' means belonging to a monastic order, not being told off; the Cistercian monks of this order keep a strict rule of silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks follow a rule that famously restricts speech, so each is a member of an order vowed to quiet.

clue.text: Tip or pour out a fragrant mixture

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to empty out a scented blend, as one might a bowl of petals.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for its perfume, a scented blend.

clue.text: Doctor is in the wrong when he is driving

indicators.note: in places one word inside another, so the short word sits within the legal wrong

blocks.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
taken as written
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A doctor is to blame for an accident that happened while behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: he is driving, so he is a car driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone who drives a car, which is what the man in the clue is doing.

clue.text: Broken boot-tree found in the garden

indicators.note: what is broken lies in pieces that can be put back in another order

blocks.note: the letters of the shoe-stretcher, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A broken wooden shoe-stretcher turns up lying in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A boot-tree is a shaped block put inside a boot to keep its form.
explanation.definitionFit: The red root vegetable is grown in vegetable gardens, so it is something found there; a loose descriptive definition.

clue.text: Vehicle of half-crazy proposer

blocks.note: surface reading: the car or carriage of some madcap suitor
setter's reading: the singer of the song Daisy Bell, who is 'half crazy' for Daisy and offers her a ride for two

explanation.walkthrough: The old music-hall song Daisy Bell runs 'I'm half crazy, all for the love of you', and the suitor offers 'a bicycle made for two'.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-wheeled machine is the vehicle the song's lovesick suitor promises Daisy instead of a stylish carriage.

clue.text: It's old, decrepit and not easily moved

indicators.note: something decrepit is falling apart, so its letters can be reassembled

blocks.note: the letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An ancient, rickety piece of furniture too heavy to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes a person who is impassive and shows little emotion, hard to stir.

clue.text: Excavate almost everything with the fingers

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the phrase loses its final letter

blocks.note: to dig is to excavate
'it all' means everything

explanation.surface: Digging out the whole lot by hand, without a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital originally means relating to the fingers, from Latin digitus, a finger.

clue.text: Prepare to fire at ducks or a bird

blocks.note: to cock a gun is to raise the hammer ready to shoot
taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: A hunter readies the gun to shoot at the ducks or some other bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' looks like the target birds; here a duck is cricket's zero, giving the letter O twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatoo is a crested parrot of Australasia, a bird.

clue.text: Quarrel in school losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the school's name is dropped

blocks.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A row breaks out at a school after the headteacher departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' looks like an argument, but it is also the bolt fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a short square-headed bolt shot from a crossbow, a kind of projectile like a shaft from a bow.

clue.text: Number in debt — but promising

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals
someone in debt is owing money

explanation.surface: A figure who is broke yet still seems to have prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promising' suggests showing potential, but it is the verb: making a vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Vowing means solemnly pledging, the same as giving a promise.

clue.text: Pile into it, though it's unsuitable

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up enclosed inside it

blocks.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth like velvet
taken as written; it is split to hold the pile

explanation.surface: Someone piles into a scrum or a heap even though it is not the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The pile is the soft surface of a fabric, called nap, and it sits inside 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not suitable or not appropriate for the purpose, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fight blows up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: raps are sharp knocks or blows

explanation.surface: A scrap breaks out and punches start flying.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, so fighting in practice or for real, and also to argue.

clue.text: Establish one's innocence but get bound over

blocks.note: first meaning: to prove someone not guilty
second meaning: to jump over an obstacle

explanation.surface: A defendant is found not guilty but still bound over to keep the peace by the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound over' is a British legal phrase for a court order to keep the peace, but here it simply means leap over.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both vindicating someone's name and leaping a hurdle without touching it.

clue.text: Signal to bring in a social worker

blocks.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
the ant is a social insect and a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: Someone gestures for a social worker to be called in to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' is the adjective meaning notable, as in a signal achievement; the social worker is an insect, not a council employee.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, signal means striking or significant, a synonym for notable or weighty.

clue.text: Weapon used to liquidate people?

blocks.note: surface reading: to kill or wipe out, as gangsters liquidate rivals
setter's reading: to make people wet by squirting liquid at them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidate' means kill, but taken as 'make liquid on' it describes a child's toy gun that squirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy gun shoots a jet of liquid, so it is a pretend weapon that soaks its targets.
